identity.name: Potassium malate
identity.chemical_class: Potassium salt of malic acid (hydroxy-dicarboxylate salt)

function.mechanism: Provides malate buffering/acidification and potassium counter-ion to adjust food pH and sourness profile.

adi.basis: No accessible finalized EFSA additive ADI for E351 was retrieved; OpenEFSA shows a 2009 nutrient-source opinion record (ON-1088).

efsa.key_finding: Potassium malate appears in OpenEFSA with a published 2009 opinion record; additive re-evaluation call information is present in EFSA search snippets but the call page returned 404 in this environment.

adi.basis: ADI not specified (group ADI for DL-malic acid and sodium/potassium/calcium salts; INS 351(i), 1982).

concerns.summary: Theoretical concern for susceptible individuals with impaired potassium handling (e.g., advanced renal disease) due to cumulative potassium intake.
Direct modern potassium-malate-specific oral toxicology studies in food-additive context were sparse in retrieved PubMed results.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA lists ADI as not specified for the malic acid/malate salts group.
No IARC classification entry was found for potassium malate or malic acid in the current IARC classifications dataset checked.

adi_exceedance.notes: Numeric ADI exceedance is not directly applicable to JECFA's 'ADI not specified' setting, but potassium load can still matter clinically in vulnerable groups.

risk_assessment.rationale: Low intrinsic hazard signal (JECFA ADI not specified; endogenous malate biochemistry; no IARC listing) but with regulatory/access gaps and sparse modern potassium-malate-specific oral safety data.
key_factors: JECFA ADI not specified for malate salts group
No explicit potassium malate listing identified in searched U.S. Title 21 CFR text
EFSA additive re-evaluation conclusion text not directly retrievable in this environment
